body.focus: Two daemon-threading tests fail under full-sweep load because they guess at timing instead of checking the property they name. (1) src/daemon/threads/__tests__/s3-acceptance.test.ts ac1 asserts session B answered within 2000 ms while A spins 4 s; the Story's LLD (86197ac6 S003 ac1) says A spins 5 s and B is answered BEFORE A's ends. Under load B's first request (which starts a new worker) took 2-3.9 s, still before A ended. Fix: spin 5 s and assert B's reply arrives before A's. (2) src/daemon/threads/__tests__/router-session.test.ts "one session's three requests reach its worker in arrival order" waits a fixed 30 ms then expects the first request started; under load the log was still empty. Fix: wait for the event (the existing `until` helper) before each positive check, keeping the fixed waits only before the "has not started" checks. Test-only; no production change; s4 ac5's 100 ms p99 bound is the acceptance criterion itself and stays.
body.summary: ac1 now checks its LLD row: A spins 5 s and B is answered before A's spin ends (no fixed bound, since B's first request also starts its worker). The router arrival-order test waits for each start with until() and keeps fixed waits only before the "has not started" checks. Both files pass 26/26 alone and 3/3 runs under 10 busy-loop processes; s4 ac5's 100 ms p99 bound is unchanged.
